p.docTitle:
EAER Ordinance
on the Minimum Requirements for Control Procedures of Protected Designations of Origin and Geographical Indications

preface.p: (Ordinance on the Control of PDOs and PGIs)

preamble.p:
The Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER)
The name of this administrative unit was amended by Art. 16 para. 3 of the Publications Ordinance of 17 Nov. 2004 (AS 2004 4937) on 1 Jan. 2013. The amendment has been made throughout the text. ,

on the basis of Article 18 paragraph 2 of the PDO/PGI Ordinance of 28 May 1997
SR 910.12 ,

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the EAER Ordinance of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3907).
item.p: carry out an initial authorisation of all production, processing and refining undertakings;
control the correct use of the traceability marks;
ensure that processing requirements are complied with;

content.p:
The certification body shall control the structural requirements in the context of the initial authorisation procedure.
Amended by No I of the EAER Ordinance of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3907).

Control procedures relating to the flow of goods, traceability and processing requirements shall take place at least every two years for each processing and refining undertaking, or every four years in the case of summer pasture holdings. For production undertakings, such procedures shall be carried out on the basis of a statistically representative random sample.
Amended by No I of the EAER Ordinance of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3907).

In the case of the Protected Geographical Indications (PGIs), testing of the final product shall be carried out once annually on the basis of a statistically representative sample of undertakings. In the case of Protected Designations of Origin (PDOs), these tests will take place at least once per year in every production, processing or refining undertaking which markets the final product. Where an undertaking markets the production of several operators, testing of the final product should be performed on a random sample of lots of each operator.
Amended by No I of the EAER Ordinance of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3907).
Undertakings where irregularities are found are subject to retesting on a systematic basis.

article.heading:
Structural and process requirements
Amended by No I of the EAER Ordinance of 29 Oct. 2014, in force since 1 Jan. 2015 (AS 2014 3907).

blockList.listIntroduction: The product specification includes the following requirements essential to the character of the product:

item.p: requirements with regard to the technical installations (structural requirements); and
requirements with regard to the production, processing and refining process (process requirements).

content.p: The traceability marking is an indelible mark which must be affixed to every individual product and which allows for the identification of the batch and the producer. Where it is not suitable to affix the label to the product itself, the traceability mark may be placed on the packaging of the product which is ready for consumption.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the EAER Ordinance of 16 Sept. 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 3289).

content.p: In the case of agricultural products and processed agricultural products, testing of the final product shall comprise physical and chemical testing, as well as an organoleptic test.
The organoleptic test is to verify the product’s conformity with the sensory description in the product specification.
In the case of forestry products and processed forestry products, testing of the final product shall comprise testing of the physical and other characteristic properties.
The responsibility for sampling is that of the certification body. The certification body is also responsible for organoleptic testing, which shall be conducted by the applicant group.

blockList.listIntroduction: The certification body shall provide an annual report to the Federal Office for Agriculture for each protected indication, containing the following information:

item.p: the list of undertakings under review, categorized by «production», «processing» and «refining»;
the total amount of products marketed with the protected indication;
the number and the type of corrective measures enacted and any suspension of certificates for each protected indication.

blockList.listIntroduction: The certification body shall ensure that it receives:

item.p: access to any documents of use to it in the context of certification.

content.p: The certification body or the certification bodies shall clarify, in a control manual, the procedures under the present Ordinance, together with the groups who have applied for registration of a PDO or a PGI.
The control manual shall be an integral component of the quality assurance scheme of the certification body or the certification bodies.
The latest version of the quality assurance scheme shall be deposited with the Federal Office for Agriculture.
This Ordinance comes into force on 1 July 1999.
